background.text: Trump has repeatedly said that Russia is somehow easier to deal with than Ukraine when it comes to negotiations. background.text: Well, Trump has said many times publicly that he believes if he has good relations with a foreign head of state, then the United States has good relations with that country. And the facts, as you described, Russia's conduct in the war, being the aggressor to begin with, those just don't matter to Trump, because after all, you want to help your friends out. So Zelensky has had a bad relationship with Trump through no fault of Zelensky's, no fault of Ukraine's, but since the famous perfect phone call in the summer of 2019 that ultimately led to Trump's first impeachment. And Zelensky's tried very hard, I think, in the past six months to get a relationship with Trump. But as we saw in the catastrophe in the Oval Office a few weeks ago, it hasn't worked. And there are people like J.D. Vance, who I think have also decided they don't like Zelensky. And don't don't like Ukraine. Vance once said in his 2022 Senate campaign, I don't care what happens to Ukraine. So it's a it's an uphill struggle, I think.

background.speaker: SPEAKER_01
background.text: Traditionally, the Republican Party has championed very strong defensive policies against U.S. adversaries like Russia. So what do you think accounts for this lack of cohesive support in the party for Ukraine?

ground_truth: Well, I think a majority of Republicans actually still support Ukraine, certainly out in the country among Republican voters, and I think quietly behind the scenes, a majority in Congress do too, but they're intimidated by Trump. It matters whether the incumbent House member, let's say, can win against a primary opponent. So it's a situation I think that's beginning to change. I think more people are beginning to speak out. I think Trump's tariff policies are causing a lot of concern, and I think that adds to concern about his really 180-degree shift toward Russia in the Ukraine. Ukraine situation, and hopefully that'll have an effect, and hopefully if some of our European allies can keep up their work to try and explain who's at fault in Ukraine and what's at stake, we're just going to have to fight it out day by day.
